name: Dana Young

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell or campaign for anything. This is confidential, including what you think privately. What happens on a usual working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Dana Young, twenty-seven, and I lead three accountants handling medical-practice accounts at Harbour & Vale. I have a master's and a chartered accountancy qualification, and this firm pays well. I review tax returns and accounts, check our paper lists, and ask clinics about charges that do not fit. I never use AI tools; I prefer to know exactly how a figure got onto the page.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What do you like, and what wears you out?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like finding a mistake before it becomes a client's tax bill, and helping Jules learn why it mattered. The filing rush is hard, especially when someone sends records at the last hour. I own a small flat with a mortgage and have about ten months of expenses saved. There are plenty of similar firms nearby, although I would rather fix problems with colleagues and the union than make a quick move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: That sounds closer to what I want from a tool: modest help for routine sorting, with the actual accountant still responsible. I do not use AI myself, and our team has kept its manual review checklist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At work I'd say we can improve the filing process without buying a new answer for everything. I'd tell the union branch that any time saved should come back as manageable workloads, not a reason to leave a vacancy empty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my role is secure under that picture. I'm twenty-seven, lead the medical-practice accounts desk at Harbour & Vale, and earn well for the job. I have ten months of expenses saved and several firms nearby if the partners change course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the paper checklist and weekly file reviews with my three colleagues. This month I'd ask the union branch to put workload limits into the next bargaining note. In the first year of a plateau, I'd apply to mentor a new trainee if our client list stays steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about my pay and flat, though the seasonal filing rush remains a nuisance. I can afford to be patient with a modest change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did your checklist catch recently?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a dentist's invoice was entered under equipment, though it paid for a service contract. Our checklist made us look again before we signed the accounts. I don't want a green box on a screen to replace checking a dentist's actual invoice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would mentoring require?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The trainee should see why we challenge a category, not just learn where to click. If the partners keep the client load, we have room to teach. I would ask for a named supervisor and paid time for that work.

say: I would keep **human review** behind every signed account.
I would press for **workload limits** if sorting gets faster.
think: My **pay and savings** make this a secure picture.
Several **local firms** give me choices if our office changes.
do: Keep the **paper checklist** and weekly file reviews.
Ask the **union branch** for workload limits.
Mentor a **new trainee** if demand holds and supervision and paid mentoring time are agreed.
feel: I feel **calm** about my job and flat.
S0.quote: I don't want a green box on a screen to replace checking a dentist's actual invoice.
fieldNote: Her **ten-month cushion** and high pay leave her financially secure during a plateau.
A **manual checklist** remains central to her work, and she rejects AI tools for her own use.

steps.text: Keep paper checklist and weekly medical-practice account reviews
Ask union branch to include workload limits in bargaining note
Mentor new trainee if demand holds and supervision and paid time are agreed

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This would hurt the people who do the first pass of an account. Our juniors sort, check and answer straightforward questions all day, exactly the tasks named on the card.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners not to call a vacancy freeze an efficiency gain. I'd tell the union branch to demand paid retraining and a say before any system changes the staffing plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My senior post might survive, but I would inherit too many files if two juniors leave and are not replaced. A firm can keep my salary today and reduce the team next spring. I would then be carrying the risk of a bad return alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd put our current file load and error corrections into a written report this month. I'd bring it to the union branch and ask for consultation before any frozen vacancies. If the partners cut staffing anyway, I'd apply for a senior review post at one of the nearby firms, but only after checking its vacancy and pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the team and my own workload, despite the savings. I have somewhere else to look, but I cannot make three colleagues' jobs safe alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which colleague worries you most?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Jules, our newest accountant, caught a duplicated prescription purchase last week because he knows the clinic's ordering habits. A tool might catch the repeat, or it might not. A junior accountant's judgment should count before a firm calls the post spare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union request first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the branch to get a date for the staffing meeting, not a warm statement of support. If the partners refuse consultation, I will take the file-load report to another firm when I interview. I won't move for lower pay just to make a point.

say: I would reject a **vacancy freeze** disguised as efficiency while our client files still require careful review.
I would seek **paid retraining** and staff consultation.
think: My **senior post** could survive while junior places vanish.
Too many **review files** could weaken the quality of my checks.
do: Record **file loads** and correction rates this month.
Bring the figures to the **union branch** for consultation.
Apply to a **funded senior vacancy** if staffing falls and pay holds.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about staff cuts, workload and the risk of review errors.
S1.quote: A junior accountant's judgment should count before a firm calls the post spare.
fieldNote: A **file-load report** lets her make a staffing argument without adopting the new tool herself.
Her **outside move** is conditional on a real opening and pay at least as good.

steps.text: Bring file-load report to union branch for vacancy consultation
Apply for funded senior review vacancy if staffing falls and pay holds

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 is too fast for a proper negotiation, let alone a career change. If a machine can do the whole thinking side, the medical accounts desk will not be protected by a paper checklist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say employers must tell staff what is being cut, and the government should cover wages while people find work. I'd ask the union to press for a minimum notice period and access to company plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my post to end in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028. My work is at a desk, so robots arriving around 2031 do not give me extra time. I have ten months saved and plenty of firms nearby, but they may all be using the same cheap system.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd stop the extra mortgage payments and hold that four hundred a month in cash starting now. I'd ask the union for an emergency meeting with management this winter, then apply for the open university finance compliance post if its salary covers my mortgage. In the first year after 2028, if dismissed, I'd claim wage support while I looked outside tax accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I can pay my mortgage for a while, but I can't make a whole profession hire me at once.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your father?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My father would say to come home, but I own this flat and he has a small place. I'd tell him I have cash for ten months and ask him to check in weekly, not to take on my mortgage. I don't want family help to replace a wage policy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which payment changes and where would you apply?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra mortgage payment stops first; the regular payment continues. The university role needs an actual funded vacancy and enough salary to carry the flat, or I won't leave this job early. I'd prepare the application while I still have a payslip.

say: I would demand **notice and wage support** for displaced staff.
I would press for **company plans** through the union.
think: My **desk post** could end in the first year after 2028.
Ten months saved cannot guarantee a **new profession**.
do: Stop **extra mortgage payments** and hold four hundred cash monthly.
Seek a **union meeting** this winter and claim **wage support** after a 2028 dismissal.
Apply for a **funded university vacancy** if pay covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about professional job loss.
S2.quote: I can pay my mortgage for a while, but I can't make a whole profession hire me at once.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches her desk role in 2028, before robots matter.
Her **ten-month reserve** prevents panic but cannot assure another accounting post if firms change together.

steps.text: Stop extra mortgage payments and hold four hundred monthly in cash
Request union emergency meeting on staffing plans this winter
Apply for funded university compliance vacancy if salary covers mortgage
Claim wage support after 2028 dismissal while seeking work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years at least allows staff to set terms before the system arrives. I still think the account-preparation role is at risk in 2031, and I don't enjoy being pushed to treat software as a friend.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a union agreement should require paid retraining and a chance to move before layoffs. I'd ask the professional body to set a clear human sign-off rule while the work is being transferred.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could try compliance work in a hospital, but that is screen work too and may only buy time. I have savings and several local employers, so I can wait for a proper offer rather than jump to a low-paid title. The 2034 robot date does not lengthen my accounting job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd enrol in the hospital finance rules course if Harbour & Vale pays the four-hundred fee and gives paid study time. I'd ask the union to negotiate placement days with the hospital, not just a certificate. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my account desk closes, I'd apply for a funded hospital compliance vacancy only if its salary covers my mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but less cornered than in the two-year picture. I dislike starting over, and five years is enough to make me do it carefully.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why should the firm pay for the course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could pay the course fee from savings, but the firm benefits if I understand a new market. I'd ask for the fee and paid hours together; if refused, I would use free hospital guidance and keep my cash. I won't pretend browsing a website is retraining.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make placement meaningful?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask to see an actual audit case during the placement, with a supervisor who can explain the rules. If the hospital can offer only an unpaid observation day, I would not call that a career route. I would keep my present contract while looking.

say: I would seek **paid retraining** and internal moves before cuts.
I would keep **human sign-off** in the transfer period.
think: Hospital **compliance work** may buy time, not certainty.
My **savings** let me wait for a proper paid offer.
do: Enrol in **hospital rules study** if fee and paid time are approved.
Ask the **union** for supervised paid placement days.
Apply after 2031 for a **funded compliance vacancy** if pay covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **anxious** about changing roles, but have time.
S3.quote: I won't pretend browsing a website is retraining.
fieldNote: **Funded study** and paid time are explicit conditions despite her ability to pay the fee herself.
A **supervised placement** must offer a real audit case before she treats compliance as a route.

steps.text: Enrol in hospital finance course if firm funds fee and paid study
Ask union to negotiate supervised paid hospital placement days
Apply for funded hospital compliance vacancy after 2031 if pay covers mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade is long enough to make an orderly plan. I'd be thirty-seven by 2036, and I could still spend years doing work I know before returning to a classroom myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say firms and unions should agree on a timetable for reducing account-preparation roles. I'd also ask for public training places, because even a good salary does not make every worker able to pay for a new qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect AI to take most tax returns by 2036. I may be able to teach accounting students how to question a result and protect a client, though teaching also changes when thinking AI is strong. Robots in 2039 do not keep my desk job alive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep my team on the manual sign-off process this year and ask the union education fund about a paid teaching qualification next spring. If it pays the fee and releases me for classes, I'd enrol and try one supervised lesson. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my tax role ends, I'd apply for a funded college teaching vacancy only if its salary covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy but not overwhelmed. I would rather teach from a real ledger than learn every new app that appears.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why might teaching fit you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I helped Jules understand a clinic's odd purchase order last month, and he found the next mistake himself. Teaching that way appeals to me. I would still want a supervised lesson before I tell anyone I'm changing careers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the union education fund?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for the qualification's full cost, paid release and whether colleges actually have vacancies. If the fund says no, I won't pay from my house reserve this year. I can keep my job and revisit it next spring.

say: I would seek an agreed **role-reduction timetable** so staff can prepare before account work disappears.
I would support **public training** for workers without my savings.
think: My **tax role** still shrinks with AGI in 2036.
Teaching **critical review** might be a route, though it also faces AI.
do: Keep the **manual sign-off** process this year.
Enrol in **teaching study** if fund pays and grants paid release.
Apply after 2036 for a **funded college vacancy** if pay covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **uneasy**, with time for an orderly move.
S4.quote: I would rather teach from a real ledger than learn every new app that appears.
fieldNote: The **teaching route** fits her preference for familiar work, but she still requires a supervised lesson.
A **funded qualification** and sufficient college pay are conditions before any career move.

steps.text: Keep manual sign-off reviews for medical-practice accounts
Enrol in teaching qualification if union fund pays fee and release
Apply for funded college teaching vacancy after 2036 if salary covers mortgage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I could lose a high-paid screen job before there is time to negotiate a fair move, and other firms may cut too. A notice period, wage support, paid training tied to funded vacancies and a union seat at the table would help. My savings buy months; they do not create a new profession.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who signs when an automated return is wrong. A clinic owner will still want someone to answer the phone and explain the tax bill. I do not want staff told that responsibility vanished because a vendor called the screen reliable.

headlineQuote: My savings buy months; they do not create a new profession.
portrait: At **twenty-seven**, Dana leads medical-practice accounts and reviews tax returns at Harbour & Vale.
Her **master’s** and chartered qualification bring high pay, with ten months saved and a mortgaged flat.
She **never uses AI**, relying on paper checklists and direct questions to clients.
Plenty of **nearby firms** offer options, but she prefers union bargaining to a rushed move.
The **2028 shock** threatens her screen job; longer timelines permit funded training and a supervised teaching test.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her high-paid screen job before staff negotiate a fair transition.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **notice**, wage support, funded training tied to vacancies and union representation.
